Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to Section 284.123(b)(l)(ii) of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (the
“Commission”) regulations,1 UGI Utilities, Inc. – Gas Division (“UGI Gas”) submits its rate
election for firm and interruptible transportation service under its Section 284.224 blanket
certificate,2 subject to refund. This filing is being made under the optional notice provisions of
Section 284.123(g).

        By way of background, on July 2, 2026, UGI Gas made a Section 284.224 filing in Docket
No. PR26-70-000. That filing addressed an increase in UGI Gas’s base rates as part of a settlement
approved by the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (“PA PUC”) on September 11, 2025.
See Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission v. UGI Utilities, Inc. - Gas Division, Docket Nos. R-
2024-3052716, et. seq. (Order entered Sept. 11, 2025). The rates were made effective on
October 28, 2025. The effective rates increased the tariff rate for the Extended Large Firm
Delivery Service (“Rate XD”) and the tariff rate for Large Firm Delivery Service (“Rate LFD”)
on file with the PA PUC, and those rates were used to support UGI Gas’s Section 284.224 rates in
the filing made July 2, 2026, in Docket No. PR26-70-000, which is pending before the
Commission. The rates submitted in Docket No. PR26-70-000 are being superseded by the rates
being submitted in this rate filing.

        UGI Gas subsequently increased its base rates as part of a second settlement approved by
the PA PUC on October 1, 2026. See Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission v. UGI Utilities,
Inc. - Gas Division, Docket Nos. R-2025-3059523, et. seq. (Order entered October 1, 2026). The
2026 settlement increases rates in a two-step process, with step 1 rates effective on October 2,
2026. The step 2 rates will become effective on October 1, 2027. The effective rates increased
the tariff rate for the Extended Large Firm Delivery Service (“Rate XD”) and the tariff rate for
Large Firm Delivery Service (“Rate LFD”) on file with the PA PUC. These newly approved and
effective step 1 rates are being used to support UGI Gas’s Section 284.224 rates in this filing, as
explained more fully below.



I.       Background

        UGI Gas is a Pennsylvania state-regulated local distribution company affiliated with and
controlled by UGI Corporation, a holding company that also owns and controls other Commission-
certificated firms (“UGI Corp.”).3 UGI Gas is organized and exists under the laws of the
Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. UGI Gas distributes and sells natural gas to commercial,
industrial, and residential consumers in Pennsylvania, subject to regulation by the PA PUC and
Maryland, subject to the regulation of the Maryland Public Service Commission. UGI Gas serves
approximately 700,000 customers, located primarily in south, central, and northeastern
Pennsylvania, and approximately 600 customers in part of one county in northern Maryland. UGI
Gas’s facilities are primarily interconnected with the interstate pipeline systems of Texas Eastern
Transmission, LP, Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C., Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line
Company, LLC, Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc., Adelphia Gateway LLC, UGI
Sunbury, LLC, UGI Mt. Bethel Pipeline, LLC, UGI Storage, Inc., UGI LNG, Inc., UGI Auburn,
LLC, and Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC, as well as local gas gathering facilities.

        UGI Gas currently holds a blanket certificate of limited jurisdiction pursuant to Section
284.224 of the Commission’s regulations, which authorizes UGI Gas to engage in the
transportation of natural gas that is subject to the Commission’s jurisdiction under the Natural Gas
Act.4 Pursuant to Section 284.123(g)(9)(iii) of the Commission’s regulations, UGI Gas is
obligated to file a rate election pursuant to 284.123(b)(l)(ii) within 30 days of the implementation
of changed rates by a state regulator. As described above, UGI Gas had new rates approved by
the PA PUC in an Order entered on October 1, 2026, with new rates effective October 2, 2026.
UGI proposes revised rates effective November 2, 2026, as described below.

II.      Rate Election

         A.      Rate XD and Rate LFD

        UGI Gas offers firm and interruptible interstate transportation service through its system.
UGI Gas has provided access to this transportation service to shippers under its current Section
284.224 certificate since October 1, 2018. Section 284.123(b)(1)(ii) of the Commission’s
regulations authorizes a Hinshaw pipeline, such as UGI Gas, to elect to use the rates contained in
one of its effective transportation rate schedules for intrastate service on file with the appropriate
state regulatory agency, which the pipeline determines covers service comparable to the
transportation service.5 Rate XD and Rate LFD are contained in UGI Gas’s PA PUC approved
tariff and both provide for transportation service that is comparable to the service that will be
provided to existing shippers and other future potential shippers. The Commission has previously
allowed Rate XD service to meet the requirements of Section 284.123(b)(1)(ii);6 in this filing, as
explained in more detail below, UGI Gas proposes to continue the Rate XD maximum rate standard
on an interim basis, and to provide for Rate LFD as a maximum rate standard going forward for
new customers.

       At the state level, Rate XD service (“Extended Large Firm Delivery Service”) is available
to any commercial or industrial gas customer seeking long term, large transportation deliveries.
Rate XD applies to UGI Gas’s entire service territory and is available to shippers that have a
prospective gas volume usage of at least 200,000 Mcf per year. Unless otherwise agreed to by the
shipper and UGI Gas, the shipper must enter into a service agreement for a minimum term of three
years. The service agreement addresses the receipt of a daily quantity of gas by UGI Gas, the
transportation of gas through UGI Gas’s facilities, and the delivery of an equivalent quantity of
gas.

        Rate Schedule LFD service (“Large Firm Delivery Service”) is similarly available to any
commercial or industrial gas customer seeking long term, large deliveries, although at lower
minimum volume levels than Rate XD. Rate LFD is available to any customer who executes a
Service Agreement with the Company for an on system Daily Firm Requirement (DFR), as agreed
to by the customer and company, for not less than fifty (50) Mcf of gas per day of firm service, for
a minimum term of two years.

         Under its Section 284.224 blanket certificate authorization, UGI Gas also provides
transportation service comparable to the Rate XD and Rate LFD services. UGI Gas uses the same
or similar facilities as its state-regulated service to provide transportation service to Marcellus
natural gas producers and gatherers who would transport more than 200,000 Mcf per year (for the
Rate XD service) or more than 50 Mcf per day (for the Rate LFD service). These shippers transport
large volumes through a portion of UGI Gas’s system to connections with interstate pipelines,
similar to Rate XD and Rate LFD end-users, though not resulting in deliveries to end-user
facilities. Similar to Rate XD and Rate LFD end-users, transportation customers establish

        UGI Gas’s other transportation tariffs are not for “comparable” service and would not be

       UGI Gas submits that Rate XD and Rate LFD are for service comparable to that requested
by transportation shippers and, therefore, are appropriate for Section 284.224 rates.

         B.      Rate XD and Rate LFD are Cost-Based Rates Approved by the PA PUC

       Rate XD and Rate LFD were approved by the PA PUC in an Order entered on October 1,
2026, in Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission v. UGI Utilities, Inc. - Gas Division, Docket
Nos. R-2025-3059523, et. al. (“2026 PA PUC Order”).

        Generally, the approved Rate XD has three elements: a customer charge, a demand charge,
and a delivery charge. In accordance with PA PUC precedent and practice, the customer charge
and maximum demand charge are determined by negotiation between the customer and UGI Gas.
The maximum average delivery charge is $1.4160 per Mcf on and after October 2, 2026.7 This
rate element was approved by the PA PUC as part of a comprehensive settlement. Id. The
settlement was supported by a cost-of-service study, proposed tariff sheets, and voluminous
discovery and testimony filed by numerous stakeholders, including testimony supporting Rate XD.
Id.

       Similarly, the approved Rate LFD has four elements: a customer charge, a maximum
demand charge, a capacity charge and a maximum distribution charge for all volumes, plus some
additional charges and riders that are inapplicable to the Section 284.224 transportation service.
The Rate LFD maximum average delivery charge is also $1.4160 per Mcf on and after October 2,
2026.8 Like Rate XD, Rate LFD was approved by the PA PUC as part of a comprehensive
settlement, id., that was supported by a cost-of-service study, proposed tariff sheets, and
voluminous discovery and testimony filed by numerous stakeholders, including testimony
supporting Rate LFD. Id.

         C.      Proposed Rates for Section 284.224 Transportation Service

        Historically, UGI Gas used only the Rate XD rates as the basis for its Section 284.224
transportation service, as is reflected in prior rate submissions and Commission orders. Following
review of the Matterhorn Rehearing Order,9 in Docket No. PR26-70-000, UGI Gas proposed to
continue offering an Interim Rate that is based on Rate XD, and that will be applicable only to
then-current customers with existing contracts for the Section 284.224 service until such time as
the existing contracts would expire; UGI proposes the same rate treatment here. For any new or
renegotiated contracts, UGI Gas is proposing a Prospective Rate that will be applicable to
customers that have executed transportation contracts on or after October 28, 2025; the Prospective
Rate, as revised by this submission, would be based on Rate LFD, as modified below.

Both firm and interruptible charges would be discountable between the minimum and maximum

        UGI Gas proposes to convert the rate to a per Dth charge, instead of the PA PUC-approved
Mcf basis, which is included in the PA PUC tariff. Therefore, UGI Gas proposes the per Dth
charge stated above, as compared to the maximum average delivery charge of $1.4160 per Mcf set
forth in its state tariff (effective on and after November 2, 2026).11 For interruptible Section
284.224 service, UGI Gas proposes to use the stated maximum delivery charge of $1.3708 per Dth
(converted by dividing $1.4160 per Mcf by the current system heat content of 1.033) on and after
November 2, 2026, and use the volumetric charge to establish a maximum firm service daily
demand charge, in order to replicate the provisions of Rate XD and Rate LFD in the state tariff.

        As illustrated above, and in the Rate Summary for firm Section 284.224 transportation
service, UGI Gas proposes a Maximum Daily Demand Charge of $1.3708 per Dth for both Rate
XD and Rate LFD, which is the maximum rate for Rate XD and for Rate LFD service in the state
tariff. The agreed-to demand charge for Rate XD in the state tariff does not have a stated ceiling;
therefore, it is not appropriate for the Section 284.224 service to include one. The Company
proposes to use the same maximum rate for interruptible service, because it does not have a rate
for interruptible Rate XD or Rate LFD service in its state tariff. Therefore, for interruptible service,
UGI Gas proposes to use the same $1.3708 per Dth rate for the Maximum Delivery Charge. This
approach is consistent with the approach currently used by UGI Gas to produce its Section 284.224
rates.

        The customer charge for Rate XD in the PA PUC-approved tariff is negotiable, as well as

Gas has not included a customer charge or the state riders for Rate XD in this rate election and
there will be no such rate element for interstate service. Rate LFD has a customer charge, as well
as certain riders12 that reflect state-related or distribution system-related costs that are also not

        UGI Gas also will not apply the retainage rate applicable under Rate XD and Rate LFD in

      The type of rate election being proposed here was initially submitted to the Commission in
Docket No. PR14-12-000 and has been previously accepted by the Commission.14

         In its Matterhorn Rehearing Order, the Commission discussed in detail the requirement
for intrastate and local distribution company rates, regarding the need to follow Straight-Fixed
Variable rate design or, in the alternative for local distribution companies, to explain and justify
any departures, inter alia.15 Historically, UGI Gas’s firm rates were a one-part rate, recovering all
fixed costs in the reservation charge. UGI Gas does not include a commodity charge and has
historically included a minimum charge of zero for the Rate XD-based service, because no
compression is used for the Part 284.224 service and there are no variable costs known to UGI Gas
at this time. However, to ensure that on a prospective basis, minimum rates reflect any potential
variable costs, the Prospective rates include a $0.0050 minimum charge for new customers and
renegotiated contracts.

III.      Language Clarifying a Term and Condition in the SOC

       The proposed non-rate revisions in the attached revised SOC tariff records involve only:
(1) a deletion in Section I.6. “Title,” clarifying title obligations; and (2) a ministerial cleanup
removal of an obsolete footer reference. The clarification in Section I.6. is consistent with the
requirements of the Commission’s regulations governing Part 284.224 transportation, under 18
C.F.R. Part 284, Subpart C, which do not require that the shipper has title to the gas being
transported. Section 1.6 states that UGI Gas’s receipt of the gas does not vest title to the gas in
UGI Gas, and the following sentence is unnecessary and potentially confusing, and is therefore
proposed to be stricken.

                       STATEMENT OF OPERATING CONDITIONS

             I.      SCHEDULE OF SPECIFIC CONDITIONS APPLICABLE
                          TO TRANSPORTATION SERVICE

1.                 AVAILABILITY

       This delivery service is available on a firm basis to any Shipper requesting transportation

service pursuant to 18 C.F.R. §284.224 and it consists of the receipt of a daily quantity of gas by

the Company from a Shipper at a specified Point(s) of Receipt along the Company’s distribution

system, the transportation of gas through the Company’s facilities, and the delivery of an

equivalent quantity of gas to a specified interstate Point(s) of Delivery. Firm service shall only

be made available by Company when it determines, in its reasonable discretion and on a non-

discriminatory basis, that such service can be accomplished by Company without detriment to

the operation of its facilities and/or Company's ability to meet its local distribution

obligations. A Shipper receiving firm service shall be limited to a maximum daily quantity

(“MDQ”).

2.                 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS

       Commission – The term Commission refers to the Federal Energy Regulatory

       Commission (“FERC”).

       Company – The term Company shall mean UGI Utilities, Inc. – Gas Division.

       Dekatherm (“Dth”) – The quantity of heat energy which is equivalent to 1,000,000 Btu.

       One "Dekatherm" of Gas means the quantity of Gas which contains one Dekatherm of heat

       energy.

       Maximum Daily Quantity (“MDQ”) – The maximum daily quantity of gas in Dths per

       day, exclusive of applicable fuel, specified in a Shipper’s Transportation Service
 Agreement that Shipper may nominate and deliver to Company at a Point of Receipt and

that Company shall deliver to a Point of Delivery.

Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) – A directive issued by the Company that is

reasonably necessary to alleviate conditions that threaten the operational integrity of the

Company’s system on a critical day, including actions necessary to comply with statutory

directives and obligations. OFOs will be communicated as soon as reasonably practical

to affected Shippers or NGSs via e-mail if the Shipper or NGSs prefer to receive notice in

this manner and provide a valid e-mail address, or if no such preference is expressed,

either electronically, by telephone, by facsimile, through the use of the media or by an

alternate mutually agreed upon method between the Company and the Shipper or NGS.

Shippers and NGSs must provide the Company with a 24-hour contact for OFOs.

Point of Delivery – The point of delivery shall be the interstate pipeline point specified

in the service agreement executed by the Company and the Shipper.

Point of Receipt – The point of receipt shall be the point specified in the service

agreement executed by Company and Shipper.

Shipper(s) – The term Shipper(s) shall mean an entity that has executed a Transportation

Service Agreement with the Company.

SOC – Refers to the currently effective Statement of Operating Conditions of the

Company.

TSA – Refers to the currently effective Transportation Service Agreement between

Company and Shipper.




                                         1
 3.                 TRANSPORTATION SERVICE AGREEMENT

       Once a service request is accepted by Company, Shipper must execute a TSA in the form

prepared by the Company specifying, amongst other things, the nature of the service (i.e., firm

service) and their MDQ. To the extent there is a disagreement between a Shipper’s TSA and the

SOC, the SOC shall prevail. This agreement shall remain in effect for the term specified therein,

or if no term is specified then indefinitely, until terminated by the Shipper or the Company upon

written notice to the other. Such termination shall be effective upon the issuance of the written

notice. Notwithstanding the above, the Company may terminate service at any time as provided

by law or by provisions of this SOC. Service will be initiated only on the first day of the calendar

month, or as agreed to by the Company.

4.                 OVERRUN SERVICE

       Provided that the transportation and delivery of such gas for any Shipper can be

accomplished by Company without detriment to the operation of its facilities and/or

Company's ability to meet its other firm obligations, Company may, upon request of Shipper

and after confirmation by the interstate pipeline to which gas is being delivered, schedule on an

interruptible basis quantities of gas in excess of Shipper's MDQ specified in its TSA. The

delivery charge for such overrun service shall be agreed upon between Company and Shipper

at the time such service is scheduled; provided however, that such charge shall not exceed

the 100% load factor volumetric equivalent of the Maximum Transportation Charge specified

in the Rate Summary. Service provided under this Section will be subject to the lowest

priority of transportation covered by the SOC. The Company will accommodate any requests

received for this service on a pro rata basis, and allocation will be done on the basis of MDQ.




                                                 2
 5.              CHARGES

     5.1        Monthly Bill. The monthly bill shall consist of the sum of billings for the

     services as provided in this Statement of Operating Conditions and subject to the

     maximum rate attached hereto (which may be discounted). For billing purposes, the gas

     received and delivered hereunder shall be measured by metering facilities installed,

     operated and maintained by Company or its designee. Volumetric measurement data

     shall be converted to thermally equivalent quantities using the actual gross heating value

     in Btu (British thermal units) per standard cubic foot dry.

     5.2        Disputed Bills. In the event that Shipper, in good faith, disputes any monthly

     bill, Shipper shall pay to Company any undisputed amount and shall notify Company in

     writing within fifteen (15) days following receipt of the invoice that Shipper disputes

     other amounts, which notice shall include adequate documentation demonstrating the

                                          RATE LFD

                                 LARGE FIRM DELIVERY SERVICE

    AVAILABILITY

    This Rate applies in the entire territory served by the Company. It is available to
    any Customer who executes a Service Agreement with the Company for an on system Daily
    Firm Requirement (DFR), as agreed to by Customer and Company in said agreement, for
    not less than fifty (50) MCF of gas per day of firm service. Volumes delivered under
    this Rate shall be metered separately from service under any of the Company's other
    rates, except as provided for in Rates IS, NNS, and MBS. In lieu of separate
    metering, the Company may accept contractual commitments specifying minimum volumes
    of service under Rate LFD.

     Service will be provided by the Company where the Customer provides suitable gas
    delivered to a Company authorized receipt point, as determined by the Company in its
    sole discretion, provided Company has available on-system and/or pipeline capacity
    available in such quantities to meet Customer requirements. The Company shall be
    under no obligation to maintain on-system facilities required for service beyond the
    term of an executed service agreement.

    Unless otherwise agreed by the Customer and Company, the Customer must enter into a
    Service Agreement for a minimum term of two (2) years. The Service Agreement shall
    continue in force for consecutive two (2) year periods unless cancelled by Customer
    upon one (1) year written notice to the Company prior to the expiration of the then
    current Service Agreement term. The Customer shall remain liable for minimum bill
    requirements for the length of the Service Agreement under this Rate, including
    applicable penalties, in the event the Customer defaults on its Service Agreement
    before the end of its term.

    Delivery Service shall be provided for all volumes provided by the Customer for     (C)
    which the Company has available delivery capacity, subject to the curtailment
    provisions of the Company's Tariff, applicable rules and regulations of the PUC and
    any other governmental mandates.

    Gas service in excess of volumes delivered by the Customer shall only be provided in
    accordance with applicable balancing provisions or in accordance with optionally
    elected and approved balancing or standby services.


    The DFR shall be the Company's contracted maximum firm delivery obligation to the
    Customer on any day and shall be no less than fifty (50) MCF. Service in excess of
    the DFR is interruptible in accordance with the terms of Rate IS.

    Service under Rate LFD is subject to the terms set forth under Section 22 - General
    Terms for Delivery Service for Rate Schedules DS, LFD, XD, and IS.

   MINIMUM BILL

   Monthly: The Minimum Monthly Bill shall be the Customer Charge, Demand Charge,
   Capacity Charge (if applicable), and Charge for Other Transportation.

   Annual: Unless a higher amount is agreed upon by the Company and Customer, the Minimum(C)
   Annual Bill shall be based on the Customer maintaining a 0.50 annual load factor and
   shall be due and payable with the bill for the 12th month in the contract year. The
   Customer's actual load factor shall be determined by dividing the total volume of gas
   taken during the contract year (including volumes taken under the Retail and Standby
   Rider, and the Cash-Out provisions of Section 22.2) by the sum of the Daily Firm
   Requirements for the contract year. If the actual load factor is less than 0.50,
   then, in addition to payment for actual usage, the Customer shall pay a Minimum Annual
   Bill charge equal to the product of: (1) the difference between 0.50 and the actual
   load factor, (2) the sum of the Customer's Daily Firm Requirements for the contract
   year, and (3) the average delivery charge paid by the Customer over the previous 12-
   month period, as calculated by the Company. If the Customer's actual load factor is
   greater than or equal to 0.50, no Minimum Annual Bill charge will be required.

   CHARGE FOR OTHER TRANSPORTATION

   If the Customer chooses to use the Company as agent in regard to transportation
   service by others, any costs calculated by or billed to the Company, with regard to
   such agency, shall be billed to the customer by the Company and may include an
   applicable administrative fee as agreed by the Customer and Company. Such charges
   related to the use of Customer elected and Company provided transportation capacity
   shall be reflected directly on the Customer’s bill for service rendered on and after
   April 1, 2024, pursuant to Commission order at Docket R-2023-3040290, with such
   charges labeled on the bill as Capacity Charge.

   CHARGE FOR UNAUTHORIZED OVERRUN

   Whenever it is necessary to restrict gas supplied under this Rate, the Company will
   provide due notice of such restriction. If a Customer, after having received due
   notice of restriction, shall take gas in excess of the amount made available by such
   notice, then the Customer shall be billed for such excess gas at the rate of Fifty
   Dollars($50.00) per MCF, or the charge calculated in compliance with Section 22.4
   Maximum Daily Excess Balancing Charge, whichever is greater, plus the charge specified
   in the monthly rate table. Section 22.4 is primarily intended to establish applicable
   daily imbalance penalty charges but shall also provide for the pricing applicable to
   any Unauthorized Overrun volumes, which shall be subject to the same pricing as an
   Intentional imbalance. Customer shall indemnify Company from any claims by third
   parties resulting from Customer's unauthorized overrun.

   SERVICE UNDER OTHER RATES

   Volumes purchased under the Retail and Standby Rider or under the Cash-Out provisions
   of Section 22.2 or taken under Rate NNS shall be included for the purposes of
   determining Excess Take Charge and Unauthorized Overrun gas.
